title: trim-and-None-on-empty closure duplicated in convert_addr and group_addresses
description: mime-tree/src/header_typed.rs:290-297 and 335-342 — the same 8-line closure name.as_ref().and_then(|s| { let trimmed = s.as_ref().trim(); if trimmed.is_empty() { None } else { Some(trimmed.to_owned()) } }) appears verbatim in convert_addr and in group_addresses. Two idiomatic fixes: (a) extract a private helper fn trim_optional(s: Option<&str>) -> Option<String>; (b) write it as a single iterator-chain expression Some(trimmed).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).map(str::to_owned). Either eliminates the duplication and makes the rule (trim → empty becomes None) visible at one site. Code duplication of business rules is exactly what the prompt's iterators/clippy guidance targets — if the trim semantics ever change, both copies must update in lockstep.
close_reason: Code cleanup batch: (.3) removed dead 'year != 0' guard in date arm and replaced comment with accurate description of what month/day == 0 catches (year mapping in mail-parser-0.11 means parts[2] is never 0 after remap); (.21) eliminated unreachable! by folding Raw and URLs handling into the same outer match as the other forms — no top-level if-and-then-match anymore; (.22) replaced split_last + unwrap_or_else with straightforward slice arithmetic via a new crlf_terminated helper returning Cow; (.23) extracted trim_or_none helper for the RFC 8621 §4.1.2.3/§4.1.2.4 display-name normalisation rule, called from both convert_addr and group_addresses.
